name: Acmer P3
tagline: Enclosed CoreXY diode with camera, sold in 24W, 48W and 10W diode + 2W IR versions
tldr: The Acmer P3 is an enclosed Class 1 laser with a CoreXY gantry at 800 mm/s, a camera covering the whole bed, 30 L/min air assist and an optional conveyor for work up to 4,000 mm long. Acmer sells it in three versions: a 24W diode from $765, a 48W diode that also runs at 24W from $1,149, and a dual-laser head with a 10W diode and a 2W infrared source for bare metal from $999 (Acmer store, October 2026). Open a version for exact specs and benchmarks.
mainObjective: Enclosed engraving and cutting at home, with a module for each kind of work

pros: Class 1 cabinet with flame detection, emergency stop and full-bed camera on every version
Three modules for three jobs: thin cuts, thick cuts, or wood plus bare metal
Priced well below xTool's enclosed S1 at each power level

ACMER Studio is serviceable but less polished than xTool's software
Smaller support network than the largest brands
beginnerNotes: This overview covers the whole Acmer P3 line. Take the 24W if you mostly engrave and cut thin wood, the 48W if thick plywood and dark acrylic cuts are the main job, and the 10W diode + 2W IR version if you also want to mark bare metal. All three share the same cabinet, camera and software.
proTips: Duct the exhaust outside or add an inline fan if you cut regularly. Use the camera for batch placement, but still run a material test matrix before production. The conveyor only pays off for long signs and strips: most buyers are better served by the rotary pack.
primaryUse: Enclosed CoreXY diode laser line for home engraving and cutting, with an infrared option for metal

editorialDepth.advantages: The P3 is Acmer's answer to xTool's S1: an enclosed, camera-equipped diode laser with a faster CoreXY gantry and a larger bed, sold for less at each power level. The module choice is the real decision: a budget 24W engraver, a 48W cutter that drops to 24W for detail, or a dual-laser head that adds bare-metal marking.
editorialDepth.limitations: Every version is still a diode: no clear acrylic, no CO₂-speed production. The stock exhaust fan and software draw the most complaints from owners, and Acmer's support network is smaller than xTool's. Check which module a pack includes before ordering: the cabinet is the same, the capabilities are not.

faq.question: Which Acmer P3 should I buy?
faq.answer: The 24W ($765) if you mostly engrave and cut thin wood; the 48W ($1,149) if you cut 10 mm and thicker plywood or dark acrylic often; the 10W diode + 2W IR ($999) if you also engrave bare metal such as stainless tags or tumblers. Prices are Basic Packs on Acmer's store in October 2026.

faq.question: Are the P3 modules interchangeable?
faq.answer: Yes. The 24W, 48W, dual-laser and 2W infrared modules fit the same P3 cabinet, and Acmer says they also fit the P2. P2 modules do not fit the P3.

moduleSystem.headline: Interchangeable laser modules on the same P3 cabinet
moduleSystem.description: The Acmer P3 is sold with a 24W diode module, a 48W module that also runs at 24W, or a dual-laser head that combines a 10W diode and a 2W 1064 nm infrared source. A 2W infrared module is also sold on its own. Modules swap on the same cabinet; only the dual-laser head carries two sources at once.
